correctness.rationale: For a compact invariant probability, stationarity of y gives E[x]=0, and stationary squared x yields a^2=(r^2-1)E[x^2]-r^2E[x^2 sin^2(dy)], excluding all compact invariant states at r<=1. The Krylov–Bogolyubov argument excludes every bounded forward orbit. Below gain one, normalization x/a produces a bounded affine recursion; direct finite-horizon squared telescoping and Jensen prove the sharp two-root speed corridor. Explicit phase-locked drifting trajectories attain its endpoints. The period-two zero-sum memory increments force x1=-x0 and B0+B1=-2, giving |x0|>=|a|/(r-1). A direct two-point cosine witness attains equality for each r>1. All assumptions, strict/equality boundaries and domain are explicit, and a symbolic/high-precision checker of the actual files passed.

value.rationale: The source investigates hidden periodic and chaotic attractors in a fixed-point-free map. Its exact coefficient threshold for the possibility of any bounded real-plane recurrence, universal sharp escape-speed interval at subcritical gain, and singular minimum recurrent amplitude above it are natural global dynamical invariants needed to interpret those numerical regimes. A constructive primitive two-cycle verifies the boundary is necessary as a family-wide obstruction. This is a sharp phase separation, not a textbook fixed-point test, renaming or arbitrary parameter slice.
